faqs.q: How long does a metal roof last on an East Orange property?

runs.v: A metal roof lasts 40 to 80 years, with copper at 70-plus years, against 20 years for 3-tab asphalt and 30 for architectural shingles, per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart; only slate, at 50 to 100 years or more, lasts longer. faqs.q: Do you need a permit for a metal roof in East Orange, NJ?

runs.v: Not for a reroof of a detached one- or two-family home, which is ordinary maintenance under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7. A commercial, multi-family, or attached roof needs a permit once more than 25% of it is repaired or replaced in 12 months, per the NJ Uniform Construction Code, which covers most East Orange metal work.

faqs.q: Why does a metal roof oil-can or buckle on an East Orange walk-up?

runs.v: A metal roof oil-cans or buckles when thermal expansion stresses a panel fastened without room to move. A clip that lets the panel float along its length resists the oil-canning and seam separation that rigid fastening causes, per Metal Construction Association guidance.

faqs.q: Should you repair or replace a metal roof in East Orange?

runs.v: Repair when the damage stays localized at seams, fasteners, or a small section; consider a full replacement when panel corrosion exceeds 20 to 25% of the area or seam-connection damage exceeds 25%, per roofing industry guidance. Recurring leaks in the same spot signal a flashing or thermal-movement defect a system-specific reseal corrects. An asphalt roof that has served East Orange weather for 20 years is near the end of its life; a metal roof at that age is barely broken in.

faqs.q: Does a metal reroof on a Register-listed East Orange building need historic approval?

runs.v: National or State Register listing alone places no restriction on a privately funded reroof, per the National Park Service. A local historic designation is a separate question, so confirm the property's status with the city before changing the roofing material.
